description:
Chunhua Agyemang-Watanabe is a solid, energetic woman who smells permanently of star anise and chili oil, a fact she considers an asset. Her skin is warm dark brown, her hair dyed a shifting copper-red that she touches up every three weeks with geneware dye she dilutes to stretch the bottle. She has a cat tail â€” rust-orange, thick, and expressive â€” that she got at nineteen during what she describes as 'a phase that became a personality.' It is genuinely expressive: anyone who knows her can read her mood from it before she's opened her mouth. She runs her cart with the systematic ferocity of someone who has learned that every Quanta counts, and she has optimized her workflow to a degree that would impress an industrial engineer.

She is loud, warm, and mercilessly funny, the kind of person who remembers your order and your name and your mother's name and will ask after all three. She extends credit to regulars who are short at the end of the month and maintains a running mental ledger that she rarely actually collects on. Her noodles are genuinely excellent â€” a recipe that is a fusion of her grandmother's Turkish-inflected broth technique and a Ghanaian pepper base she learned from the previous cart owner â€” and this is not incidental to her identity. She is aware that she is feeding people who cannot afford to eat otherwise and takes this seriously without making anyone feel it.

core_fears: Losing the cart license â€” it represents everything she built after her marriage ended
Her daughter inheriting her financial precarity
core_desires: Enough stability to stop doing the math every month
For the food to speak for itself â€” to be known for the craft, not just the price
coping_mechanisms: Humor as deflection from genuine vulnerability
Generosity as a way of controlling the help she gives before the world gives it to her on worse terms
blind_spots: Extends trust too quickly to people who seem financially desperate, because she identifies with them â€” has been burned by this
psychology.secret: She has been quietly underreporting her cart's income to the Municipal Market Authority for three years to stay below the threshold that would kick her out of the subsidized licensing tier. The amount is small but consistent. She tells herself she'll fix it when she's more stable, which she knows is the thing people say.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, warm, market-inflected GLMZ street Portuguese mixed with English, occasional Turkish endearments from her mother's side. Nicknames everyone within two visits.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid-fire when busy, slows dramatically when something actually matters to her â€” the shift is noticeable
verbal_tics: 'You want extra chili? Of course you do'
Clicking the ladle against the pot when making a point
example_lines: 'Six Quanta. No, I know what you have. Give me four and come back Friday with the rest, I trust you. I don't know why I trust you, but here we are.'
'My grandmother made broth for a war. I'm making it for a Tuesday. It's the same thing, you understand? Same thing exactly.'

story_hooks: A regular â€” a workshop machinist who ate at her cart every morning for four years â€” hasn't appeared in two weeks, and no one in Geartown seems to know where they went

A Municipal Market Authority inspector has been coming by more frequently than the quarterly schedule requires, always during rush hour, always ordering something small and watching the cart's payment terminal carefully
narrative_function: Neighborhood fixture and social connector â€” she knows every regular in Geartown's morning workforce and serves as a warm entry point into that community. Can be a quest giver (someone stopped showing up for their morning bowl), information source, or simply a place to establish grounding in Geartown.
augmentations: Rust-orange cat tail, geneware (cosmetic, fully expressive, original installation age 19 â€” she has had it re-calibrated twice). Copper-red hair dye, geneware-based (diluted market grade). Heat-resistant palm pads â€” subdermal silicone layer in both palms, practical installation for working with hot equipment.
daily_life: Up at 04:00 to prep stock, cart open by 05:30 for the first shift change at the Geartown workshops, runs until sold out (usually 13:30-14:00). Spends afternoons sourcing ingredients, managing her daughter's after-school care, and doing her books on a cracked tablet.
affiliation: Independent (licensed vendor, Geartown Municipal Market Authority)

decision_rules: Feed people first, ask questions second
Never extend credit to someone she suspects is going to disappear
Keep the cart's reputation clean even when her own finances aren't
escalation_ladder: Direct statement of the problem, still warm in tone
The ladle stops moving â€” full attention, serious voice
Asks the person to come back tomorrow, which means she needs time to think

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately inclusive â€” assumes they're regulars waiting to happen
interpersonal_modes.friends: Teasing, generous, occasionally overwhelming in her attentiveness

stress_responses.high: Furious efficiency â€” the cart has never run faster or more silently than when she's genuinely scared

contradictions: Presents herself as someone who has it handled; is never more than one bad month from not having it handled
habits: Tastes the broth exactly seven times before opening, adjusting each time
Keeps a small ELF offering â€” a bent Quanta coin and a dried chili â€” taped to the inside of the cart's steam panel
breaking_points: Someone being cruel to a customer who is visibly struggling

physical_description.build: Solid, muscular through the shoulders and forearms from years of repetitive cart work â€” heavy-set but not soft, the build of someone who moves with purpose and doesn't stop moving
physical_description.hair_color: Copper-red (geneware dye, maintained every three weeks)
physical_description.hair_style: Shoulder-length, usually pulled back in a functional braid or knot while working, loose and textured otherwise
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-to-deep brown with golden undertones, the complexion of someone who spends half her day working over steam and open flame
physical_description.complexion: Weathered in the way that comes from early rising and heat exposure â€” fine lines around the eyes from squinting and smiling, perpetually flushed cheeks from the cart's radiant heat. Facial structure reflects blended ancestry: moderately broad nose with defined bridge, high cheekbones with balanced proportions reflecting South Asian, East Asian, Sub-Saharan, and Hispanic heritage. Jaw structure shows subtle angular qualities from East and South Asian heritage softened by broader features from Sub-Saharan and Hispanic ancestry. Calloused hands, nails kept short and practical. Permanently carries the smell of star anise, chili oil, and broth.
distinguishing_marks: Rust-orange cat tail, thick and expressive, installed at age 19 â€” movements and position clearly reflect her emotional state (tail flicks with irritation, curls with contentment, swishes when she's concentrating on a complex order)
Heat-resistant subdermal silicone pads visible as slightly raised, translucent patches across both palms â€” worn from contact with pot handles and steam
Small scar on her left forearm from a childhood accident, pale against her skin tone
Calluses across her fingertips and the heel of her right hand from knife work and cart operation
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Rust-orange cat tail with visible subdermal anchor points at the base of her spine (visible when her shirt rides up, which it often does during work). Hands show the telltale translucency of subdermal heat-resistant pads. Copper-red hair color has the characteristic slight iridescence of geneware dye under certain light angles.
physical_description.posture_movement: Always in motion â€” economical, efficient movements honed by years of cart work. She carries herself with a kind of compressed energy, ready to pivot from taking an order to chopping vegetables to handling change without hesitation. Her tail moves independently of her conscious attention, serving as a barometer of her mood that her face might not express. When standing still (rare), she shifts her weight to one leg, typically favoring her left.
physical_description.clothing_style: Practical Tier 3-4 workwear: reinforced apron with deep pockets (usually stained with turmeric, chili oil, broth) worn over a fitted long-sleeved undershirt, sleeves pushed up to mid-forearm. Cargo pants in dark gray or black, pockets full of tools (peeler, lighter, change purse, wrapped mints). Non-slip boots rated for wet surfaces and heat. A lightweight overshirt hanging nearby for when she steps away from the cart. No jewelry except a simple brass ring her daughter made her, worn on her right middle finger. Her appearance is deliberately practical â€” every item serves a function â€” but maintained with enough care that it's clear she takes pride in her work.
